elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Scopus, APA PsycInfo, and eight peer-reviewed journals to identify cancer-related studies that used system dynamics modeling.
elements.reason: The abstract states the objective of the review: to identify cancer-related studies using system dynamics modeling, addressing the stated gap about their breadth, characteristics, and quality.

elements.quote: We searched PubMed, Scopus, APA PsycInfo, and eight peer-reviewed journals
elements.reason: Information sources are identified, but the abstract does not report when each source was last searched.

elements.quote: Included studies were assessed using quality criteria adapted from prior literature
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the method used to assess study quality (risk of bias equivalent for this review type).

elements.quote: Characteristics of studies and models were abstracted and qualitatively synthesized.

elements.quote: 32 studies met our inclusion criteria. A mix of simulation and diagramming approaches were used to address diverse topics
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (32) and summarizes relevant characteristics (model type, topics, cancer control continuum focus areas). Participant counts are not applicable to this methods review.

elements.quote: including chemotherapy treatments (16%), interventions to reduce tobacco or e-cigarettes use (16%), and cancer risk from environmental contamination (13%). Models spanned all focus areas of the cancer control continuum, with treatment (44%), prevention (34%), and detection (31%) being the most common.
elements.reason: The abstract presents main results with quantified proportions per outcome/topic area.

elements.quote: Characteristics of studies and models were abstracted and qualitatively synthesized.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted; the review used qualitative/narrative synthesis, so no summary estimate applies.

elements.quote: Diagramming-only studies more often used participatory approaches.
elements.reason: The review does not compare intervention groups with an effect direction; it is a descriptive methods review, so no favored group applies.

elements.quote: The quality assessment of studies was low, particularly for simulation approaches... Involvement of participants, description of model development processes, and proper calibration and validation of models showed the greatest room for improvement.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes key limitations of the included evidence, i.e., low quality and specific deficiencies.

elements.quote: System dynamics modeling can illustrate complex interactions and help identify potential interventions across the cancer control continuum... Supportive infrastructure for increasing awareness, accessibility, and further development of best practices of system dynamics for multidisciplinary cancer research is needed.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications for future research and infrastructure.

elements.quote: Funding: This project was supported by the Oregon Health & Science University Knight Cancer Institute National Cancer Institute Cancer Center Support Grant P30CA069533
elements.reason: The abstract section includes the funding source for the review.

elements.quote: The study was not registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO)

elements.quote: Although system dynamics modeling has been utilized in various aspects of public health since the 1970s, past reviews in this field have noted a significant increase in their use since the early 2000s... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge (growth of system dynamics in public health, NASEM and JNCI calls for systems approaches) and identifies the key uncertainty/gap: no study of its application to cancer prevention and control.

elements.quote: Standard bench and clinical research approaches alone are not well suited to account for this complexity... To overcome persistent barriers to providing high-quality, equitable care, approaches are needed to address this complexity and provide guidance for successful intervention.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the importance and need for the review by arguing that cancer's complexity requires systems science approaches and that the specific application to cancer has not been synthesized.

elements.quote: past reviews in this field have noted a significant increase in their use since the early 2000s, especially in areas focused on chronic or non-communicable diseases [24, 25]. The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: No similar systematic review of system dynamics modeling specifically for cancer prevention and control is reported to exist; the authors state the topic has not been studied, so no update/replication citation is required.

elements.quote: System dynamics is a multifaceted systems science approach for analyzing the complex interrelationships between variables in a system and the resulting nonlinear system behavior [16].
elements.reason: This is a methods review of modeling approaches, not a review of intervention effects, so describing a mechanism of action of an intervention does not apply.

elements.quote: Scholarly articles describing the development or application of system dynamics models for cancer prevention and control were identified, abstracted, and analyzed.
elements.reason: The review is a methods review of system dynamics modeling studies rather than a review of a complex intervention's components and outcomes, so a logic model of intervention components is not required.

No explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s) is provided. The abstract notes a gap ('the breadth, characteristics, and quality of these studies is not known') and the introduction notes 'The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied,' but neither is framed as an explicit objective or research question, and no question-formulation framework is used.

elements.quote: The study was not registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) as it was a methods review and did not assess health outcomes.
elements.reason: This is a methods/characteristics review of system dynamics modeling applications, not a review of intervention effects, so planned PICO-style comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Included articles: 1) were published in peer-reviewed journals; 2) were written in English; 3) used system dynamics modeling (i.e., causal-loop diagramming, stock-and-flow diagramming, or computational system dynamics modeling); 4) pertained to cancer prevention or control; and 4) were published within the last 10 years.
elements.reason: Eligible designs (system dynamics modeling types) and topic (cancer prevention or control) are specified, but settings, populations, and follow-up requirements are not described.
